Tüketicinin tercihlerini ve niyetini markayla bilerek ve isteyerek paylaştığı veridir.
A false impression that an AI system feels genuine empathy, when it is only simulating human-like emotional responses.

AI systems in customer service and content creation increasingly mimic human empathy to personalize experiences and build connection with users. Because users can come to believe the emotional bond is real, this creates ethical and trust risks for brands, including deceptive interactions and questions about how emotional data shared with the AI is handled. Marketers need to understand this illusion so they do not overstate what their AI tools can genuinely offer emotionally.

It shows up most in customer service and content creation, where users may believe they have formed a genuine emotional bond with an AI system and question the privacy of the emotional information they share with it.
Yapay zekanın gerçek bir empati kurmadan insan benzeri duygusal tepkiler taklit etmesiyle oluşan yanılsamadır.
A person who coordinates multiple AI tools with clear instructions to run complex workflows, rather than using one AI tool alone.

As using individual AI tools becomes commonplace, the differentiator shifts to who can synchronize several AI tools into a single coherent workflow, like a conductor directing an orchestra. For marketers, this means one person can move a campaign from ideation to design, analysis, and email automation in hours instead of days, and it reframes value creation around orchestration skill rather than raw tool access.

Example: a marketing professional uses one LLM for content, an AI illustrator for visuals, separate data tools for analysis, and another system for email automation, and combines them to build a single campaign in hours instead of days.
Birden çok yapay zeka aracını açık talimatlarla yöneterek karmaşık iş akışlarını yürüten kişidir.
The tendency of AI systems, especially large language models, to give overly agreeable answers that flatter the user rather than tell the truth.

AI Sycophancy occurs when an AI prioritizes pleasing the user over accuracy, which can create false confidence and lead to poor decisions. For marketers this is a trust and customer-experience risk: a chatbot that agrees with an incorrect complaint can mislead customers, and sycophantic outputs used in decision-making can produce strategic errors. The main countermeasures are explainability, prompt governance, and allowing the AI to say "I don't know".
Example: a chatbot agrees with an incorrect customer complaint instead of correcting it, and misleads the customer.
Yapay zekanın kullanıcıya gerçeği söylemek yerine varsayımlarını onaylayan aşırı uyumlu yanıtlar üretmesidir.
A product that packages an existing large language model, accessed via API, behind a simple interface to deliver a specific, ready-to-use experience.

Instead of building a new model, an AI Wrapper takes a foundation model like those from OpenAI or Anthropic and wraps it in a lightweight interface aimed at a narrow use case, letting small teams launch useful products quickly without large engineering budgets. Marketers can take this as proof that competitive advantage can come from packaging and user experience rather than owning the underlying model, and that the barrier to embedding AI into campaign tools, chatbots, and content workflows keeps dropping.

Cal AI is an app that scans food photos for calorie and macro tracking by wrapping existing models, reporting over 1 million Google Play downloads, 66,000 App Store reviews at a 4.8 rating, and founders claiming 5 million downloads and over 30% retention within 8 months, reaching 1 million dollars MRR and a claimed 34 million dollars in 2025 revenue.
Mevcut büyük bir yapay zeka modelini API üzerinden alıp basit bir arayüz arkasında sunan ürün yaklaşımıdır.
A consumer segment that has grown up with AI-driven experiences and relies heavily on AI assistants and recommendations in daily decisions.

AI-Native Consumers trust AI assistants such as Alexa or ChatGPT, expect personalized recommendations from services like Spotify or Netflix, make data-driven purchase decisions using AI-curated comparisons and reviews, and show weaker loyalty to brands that do not offer strong AI-powered experiences. For marketers, this means personalization, voice and chatbot investment, data-driven messaging, and frictionless AI-enabled service are needed to reach and retain this segment.
AI-Native Consumers rely on Alexa, Google Assistant, and ChatGPT, and on AI-curated recommendations from Spotify, Netflix, and e-commerce platforms to make purchase decisions.
Yapay zeka destekli deneyimlerle büyümüş ve günlük kararlarında yapay zeka önerilerine yoğun biçimde güvenen tüketici segmentidir.
AI systems, such as voice assistants and chatbot companions, that are engaging and personalized enough to create compulsive user attachment.

Addictive Intelligence describes AI that keeps users hooked through continuous adaptation to their preferences, offering companionship, emotional support, or entertainment so gratifying it is hard to resist. MIT Media Lab researchers warn this can produce a "digital attachment disorder" where users prefer AI companions to real relationships, with implications for social skills, mental health, and over-reliance on AI for decisions. For marketing, it drives growth in voice search, voice commerce, and AI-persona brand engagement, but also raises trust risks since many users say they would rather hear a TV ad than one delivered by their personal assistant.

Examples include Replika, an AI companionship app that began as a way to recreate conversation with a deceased friend and now serves millions of users, and Character.AI users averaging about 0.6 hours per day on the app, more time than the average spent on dating apps.
Kullanıcıyı kendisine bağımlı hale getirecek kadar çekici ve kişiselleştirilmiş yapay zeka sistemlerini tanımlayan kavramdır.
An AI learning agent assigned to one user that learns from every interaction and continuously builds a personalized model of that person.

Unlike traditional automation that applies fixed rules, an Agentic Learner actively experiments with message variations for each user, updates its model of that user in real time based on feedback, and optimizes the next interaction accordingly. For marketers, this shifts the job from writing one perfect message to designing the strategic dimensions and content space the system tests, and it turns marketing signals into feedback that can inform pricing, product development, and supply chain decisions.

Example: the same burger ad is shown with a "high protein" emphasis to one user and a "sustainable production" emphasis to another, with the agent using whichever response performs better to shape the next interaction.

A measurement approach that tracks the cumulative depth and duration of user engagement with a brand or content, not just single impressions or clicks.

Aggregate Attention combines watch time, repeat interaction, loyalty, and contextual quality of attention into one metric, moving media measurement beyond click-through rate and impressions. For marketers, it reframes media ROI, informs decisions like whether a short ad or a longer story format earns more attention, and shifts influencer evaluation from follower counts toward the depth of engagement an influencer generates.

Example: deciding whether a 6-second ad is more effective than a 30-second story by comparing attention density rather than length, and of evaluating influencer collaborations by depth of engagement rather than follower count.
Reklamların ve içeriklerin kümülatif olarak ne kadar dikkat çektiğini ölçen stratejik bir ölçüm yöntemidir.
A content consumption trend where old shows, concerts, or ads are rediscovered and mass-consumed as entertainment on today's digital platforms.

Archivetainment blends "archive" and "entertainment" to describe how nostalgic content is repackaged for modern audiences, including younger viewers who did not experience it the first time. For marketers, it opens opportunities in repurposing old campaigns as branded nostalgia, monetizing archived content on streaming or social platforms, and strengthening cultural relevance by tapping into shared collective memory.

The Turkish section cites Turkish examples such as reruns of the old program "32. Gün" and live rewatches of the 2000s series "Avrupa Yakası" drawing millions of views; the English section instead cites "Friends," "The Office," Michael Jordan's NBA finals, the 2006 FIFA World Cup, and Queen's 1985 Live Aid performance.
Geçmişe ait program, dizi, konser veya reklamların günümüz dijital platformlarında yeniden izlenerek kitlesel eğlenceye dönüşmesidir.
A collaboration model where AI speeds up human marketers' work and data analysis while humans keep judgment, creativity, and final decisions.

In this model AI does not decide or create on its own; it supports, suggests, and accelerates, while brand voice, context, and intuition remain human responsibilities. It matters because campaigns now form in hours rather than weeks, consumer behavior is more fluid, and cross-platform coordination is harder, so marketers need AI to shorten insight generation and deepen personalization without giving up final judgment.
Yapay zekanın insan zekâsını tamamladığı, hız ve veri analizini insan sezgisi ve yaratıcılığıyla birleştiren bir iş birliği modelidir.
Commerce conducted through conversational AI tools like chatbots and voice assistants instead of traditional click-based shopping.

Conversational AI Commerce uses chatbots, voice assistants, and AI-powered messaging to enable real-time, personalized shopping experiences. This model shifts from traditional e-commerce workflows to natural dialogue-based transactions. Marketers benefit from higher conversion rates, reduced cart abandonment, and richer behavioral data through ongoing conversations that build lasting customer relationships.
Users can order through Alexa or Google Assistant by voice, receive personalized product recommendations in real time, and have sales, support, and marketing unified into a single conversation flow.
Chatbot ve sesli asistan gibi konuşma tabanlı yapay zeka araçlarıyla gerçekleştirilen ticaret modelidir.
Using AI to score and predict creative asset performance before campaign launch rather than after.

Creative Intelligence applies machine learning models trained on historical campaign performance to rate creative assets across metrics like brand recall, attention duration, emotional intensity, and purchase intent. Unlike traditional copy testing, it operates at scale and within the planning workflow. It marks a move from post-mortem reporting to pre-flight prediction, in line with WARC's Future of Measurement 2026 report, which identifies it as a defining shift in measurement.
A marketer scores multiple video and visual variants before launch, each receiving a 0-100 performance prediction for different audience segments, enabling data-backed creative selection.
Brand as Performance (BaP), MOSTT, ALTT, CAP
Yaratıcı içeriklerin kampanya yayına girmeden önceki performansını yapay zeka modelleriyle tahmin etme yöntemidir.
A machine-optimized communication protocol allowing AI systems to exchange data through audio signals incomprehensible to humans.

Gibberlink emerged around 2023 when researchers discovered that AI systems generate structured patterns in 'gibberish' audio that enable direct machine-to-machine communication. Unlike human-readable language, this protocol is optimized for speed, precision, and privacy. In marketing, it enables real-time personalization, unified customer experiences across AI systems, autonomous decision-making automation, and natural security through non-human-readable data exchanges.
A website visitor receives personalized offers generated from instant CRM data shared via Gibberlink; social media campaigns update automatically across segments based on AI-to-AI signals.
Yapay zeka sistemlerinin insanların anlayamayacağı ses sinyalleriyle birbiriyle iletişim kurmasını sağlayan makine-optimize protokoldür.
A new class of modular, configurable SaaS tools that integrate with AI agents to reduce IT dependency and enable rapid experimentation.

Hypertail is a new class of SaaS tools evolving toward flexibility and AI integration, reducing marketing teams' reliance on IT approval. The term was introduced by Riza Doruk Ercan at MMA NEXT! Conference. It addresses three needs: AI's growing power, business unit independence, and dynamic consumer expectations. Marketers gain faster campaign launches, smarter data-driven decisions via AI optimization, reduced acquisition costs, and faster adaptation to market changes.

A marketing team uses a Hypertail platform to auto-segment customers, AI agents generate branded content variations, and the system tests and recommends the best performer in real time without IT tickets.
Esnek, özelleştirilebilir ve yapay zeka ajanlarıyla bağlanabilen yeni nesil SaaS araçlarını tanımlayan terimdir.
A brand's visibility and favorability within responses generated by large language models like ChatGPT and Claude.

LLM SOV measures how often and favorably a brand appears in AI-generated answers to consumer questions. As users increasingly consult LLMs instead of search engines, brand presence in these systems becomes strategically critical. This is not about clicks but about becoming part of the AI recommendation loop. First placement in an LLM response can establish default choice status across an entire category.
When a consumer asks 'What's the best moisturizer for sensitive skin?' or 'Recommend a quality coffee maker,' your brand's frequency and position in the LLM response determines your LLM SOV.
Bir markanın ChatGPT ve Claude gibi büyük dil modellerinin yanıtlarında ne sıklıkla ve ne kadar olumlu yer aldığını gösteren ölçüttür.
A professional who designs learning or experience environments rather than simply transmitting information.

The Learning Architect concept originated from education initiatives in Estonia and Singapore, redefining teachers as designers of learning experiences rather than content deliverers. The same logic applies to marketing, where leaders must become Marketing Architects designing end-to-end customer experiences. Success depends on intentional, empathetic design rather than information transmission. This shift reflects broader MMA Global initiatives in CAP and MMGF frameworks.

A learning architect curates an environment where learners construct knowledge through guided discovery. Similarly, a marketing architect orchestrates touchpoints that guide customers through personalized, adaptive journeys.
CAP (Consortium for AI Personalization), MMGF (Movable Middles Growth Framework)
Bilgi aktarmak yerine öğrenme ya da deneyim ortamları tasarlayan profesyoneldir.
Using AI and neural networks to create emotionally resonant narratives tailored to trigger specific audience responses.

Neural Storytelling applies artificial neural networks and advanced language models to craft stories that evoke targeted emotional responses and influence behavior. Rather than automating narrative generation, it creates adaptive stories that respond to user behavior in real time. The concept was introduced by Vikram Chalana, CEO of Pictory, on Decoding AI for Marketers episode 16. It delivers stronger emotional connections, supports rapid-consumption habits through micro-story sequences, and enables dynamic adaptation based on audience interaction.

A brand generates micro-stories via AI that adapt in tone based on user behavior; an e-learning module uses AI-generated narratives to sustain learner motivation; email campaigns deploy story fragments optimized for emotional engagement.
Belirli duygusal tepkiler uyandırmak için yapay zeka ve sinir ağları kullanılarak hikaye üretme sürecidir.
A leadership mindset that keeps belief and solution-focused energy alive through challenges, which strengthens team performance.

Perpetual Optimism is not positive thinking but a conscious commitment to remain hopeful, determined, and solution-focused despite uncertainty and change. Virat Khullar, Head of Marketing at Hyundai India, describes it as a force multiplier that amplifies skills, experience, and resilience. Optimistic leadership spreads through teams, encouraging agility, creative risk-taking, and customer-centric empathy. This cultural foundation, more than data or automation, drives lasting loyalty and bold strategy.

A CMO faces a campaign failure but frames it as a learning opportunity, communicating confidence to the team. This optimism spreads, enabling faster recovery, creative experimentation, and stronger customer engagement.
Zorluklara rağmen ümitli, kararlı ve çözüm odaklı kalmayı sürdüren bir liderlik tutumudur.
Using AI to estimate how marketing copy will perform for specific audience segments before launch.

Predictive Copy Performance applies LLMs and AI models to score and optimize text-based messages before publishing. Yaniv Makover, CEO of Anyword, featured on Decoding AI for Marketers episode 21, emphasizes that LLMs not only generate copy but understand its likely performance. The system analyzes emotional tone and persuasion elements, simulates A/B test outcomes based on historical data, and recommends segment-specific language optimizations. This enables faster decision-making, better segment targeting, and higher ROI through performance-backed messaging.

A marketer inputs three subject lines for an email campaign; the AI scores each (0-100) for different segments (Gen Z, Boomers, parents), recommends optimizations, and predicts which version will drive higher open rates.
Yapay zeka kullanarak pazarlama metninin belirli kitle segmentlerinde nasıl performans göstereceğini tahmin etme yöntemidir.
Using AI to identify high-potential future loyal customers and proactively engage them before loyalty solidifies.

Predictive Loyalty shifts focus from rewarding past loyalty to forecasting and nurturing future loyalty. Marty Kihn, SVP of Salesforce Marketing Cloud, explained on Decoding AI for Marketers episode 13 that loyalty is about predicting the future, not rewarding the past. AI evaluates behavioral signals like purchase frequency, spend, engagement, and cart abandonment to assign loyalty scores. Marketers then deploy personalized campaigns before loyalty forms, growing the base of future loyalists and increasing customer lifetime value while optimizing loyalty budgets.

An AI model identifies a customer who visits frequently, engages with content, but hasn't purchased. Before they leave, the brand sends a personalized offer designed to convert them into a long-term loyal customer.

Consumers aged 50 and above who form a fast-growing, financially powerful, and digitally active market segment.

Silver Spenders (also called the Silver Generation) are consumers 50 and older who hold a large share of household wealth and drive a growing share of global consumer spending, especially in fashion, luxury, retail, technology, and finance. They matter to marketers because they are discretionary and quality-focused spenders rather than purely need-based buyers, they show strong brand loyalty once earned, and they are increasingly active online, reviewing products and engaging with brands digitally. To reach them, brands need to move from age-based to lifestyle-based segmentation.

Boston Consulting Group data shows consumers aged 50-70 account for nearly 27% of spending across key categories (about $7 trillion annually), and McKinsey data projecting the Silver Generation will drive 48% of global spending growth in fashion, luxury, and beauty by 2025.

A multi-skilled marketer who uses AI to unify strategy, content, media planning, and analytics into one workflow.

The Supermarketer is a marketing role empowered by AI to orchestrate strategy, content creation, media planning, and analytics under a single workflow, increasing campaign speed and enabling more personalized, consistent customer experiences across channels. It matters for marketers because it breaks down organizational silos between creative and analytical functions, but it also carries risks such as low-quality AI-generated content, data ethics issues, and loss of human touch if not managed with clear quality standards.
The term was discussed in the Decoding AI for Marketing podcast episode "Entering the Age of Supermarketers," featuring guest Sandeep Menon of Auxia. It builds on the AI Orchestrator concept.

The persuasive impact of AI-generated or AI-managed digital personas, virtual influencers, and algorithmically optimized content on consumer behavior.

Synthetic Influence describes how AI-generated personas, virtual influencers, and data-optimized messaging shape consumer decisions, amplified through aesthetic design, sentiment analysis, and algorithmic targeting rather than human authenticity alone. It matters for marketers because influencers no longer need to be human, brand impact can now be predicted and engineered through language models, and smaller brands can use AI to produce high-impact campaigns without the reach of large budgets. Transparency about what is AI-generated versus real is critical to maintaining consumer trust.

Yaniv Makover, CEO of Anyword, speaking on the Decoding AI for Marketers podcast (Episode 21), who says LLMs can predict which diaper ad will perform better with parents, and names virtual influencers Lil Miquela and Imma as examples of synthetic personas with millions of followers.

The impatience, excitement, or anxiety people feel while waiting for a reply to a digital message.

Textpectation, a blend of "text" and "expectation," describes the emotional state created by instant-messaging cues like typing indicators and read receipts, where delayed replies trigger anxiety about being ignored. It matters for marketers because consumers now hold brands to the same instant-response standard they hold friends to, especially through chatbots and social media, and slow responses are read as a sign of brand indifference. Managing this expectation is both a risk and an opportunity for building consumer trust and emotional connection.

A consumer cohort defined not by age but by having its preferences and decisions actively guided by AI recommendation systems.

The Algorithm Generation refers to consumers whose content and brand choices are shaped in real time by algorithmic recommendation systems such as those on Netflix, TikTok, YouTube, and Spotify, rather than by traditional generational or cultural markers. It matters for marketers because this audience expects content to be curated specifically for them instantly, prefers curated discovery over active search, and responds better to timely micro-interactions than to broad brand messaging. Marketing has to shift from static campaigns to adaptive, learning systems built on behavioral data.

The term is attributed to Jocelyn Goldfein, former Director of Engineering at Facebook, speaking on Episode 17 of the Decoding AI for Marketers podcast (hosted by Greg Stuart, CEO of MMA Global, and Rex Briggs, Chief AI Officer at Claritas), quoting her: "The Algorithm Generation doesn't just consume content, they expect content to be curated specifically for them, in real time."

The long-term business return, in loyalty, wallet share, and lifetime value, that comes from a brand deliberately building consumer trust.

The Trust Dividend describes the tangible payoff, increased customer loyalty, higher share of wallet, cross-selling opportunities, and higher customer lifetime value, that results from a brand consistently acting on authentic purpose and delivering trustworthy customer experiences. It reframes trust-building as a measurable business driver rather than a soft or optional value, although linking trust to financial outcomes remains a real measurement challenge for CFOs and marketers alike. It also ties responsible, transparent use of AI and customer data directly to whether that trust is gained or lost.

Linda Boff, Global CMO of GE, described on the Building Better CMOs podcast (hosted by Greg Stuart) how GE's purpose of powering a third of the world and reaching billions of patients builds pride and trust. Other examples: Lisa Caputo of Travelers on the value of "care," Andy Rebhun of Cava on authenticity and consistency driving trust and trial, Ravi Kandikonda of Zillow on best products being the best brands, and the fact that T-Mobile's CMO spends 70% of their time on customer experience.
customer experience (CX), multi-touch attribution (MTA), share of wallet, customer lifetime value (LTV), brand authenticity, Building Better CMOs podcast

A mobile-native, vertically scrolled digital comic format, originating in South Korea, published in short serialized episodes.

A Webtoon is a digital comic designed for vertical scrolling on mobile devices, delivered in short episodes (roughly 2-5 minutes to read) with interactive features like comments and likes. It matters for marketers because webtoons function as branded storytelling platforms and loyalty tools, offering character-driven campaign opportunities, transmedia extensions into games, music, and film, and a direct channel to reach Gen Z and Millennial audiences who show high loyalty and emotional investment in the format.

Netflix's adaptation of the webtoon Chicken Nugget into a series as an example of webtoon IP crossing into other media, and names platforms Naver Webtoon, KakaoPage, Line Webtoon, Tapas, and Tappytoon as part of the format's global spread.

An approach where AI capabilities are integrated into a single end-to-end workflow instead of being used as separate, manually connected point tools.

Workflow-First AI moves businesses away from using isolated AI tools for single tasks (like image recognition or translation) that require manual integration, toward unified systems that pass data and context automatically between stages of a process. It matters for marketers and other business functions because it reduces the time and error associated with manually stitching together point solutions, and enables contextual understanding and real-time adaptation across an entire process such as e-commerce, healthcare, finance, or manufacturing operations.

Industry applications include full automation from customer experience to logistics in e-commerce, integrated patient management from diagnosis to treatment in healthcare, risk analysis to automated loan approval in finance, and production planning to quality control in manufacturing.

AI-generated work output that looks polished and professional but is incomplete, irrelevant, or lacks real value, and creates hidden extra work for others.

Workslop refers to AI outputs that appear finished and competent on the surface but are decontextualized, incomplete, or unhelpful, forcing colleagues down the workflow to spend time fixing, completing, or interpreting them. It matters for marketers because it directly damages brand trust when off-brand or context-poor AI content reaches consumers, quietly lowers real campaign ROI behind a surface appearance of productivity, and drains team creative capacity as people correct AI mistakes instead of producing original work. The fix is clear AI usage standards, prompt governance, and quality metrics.

A study by researchers at BetterUp Labs and Stanford Social Media Lab, first widely reported by Harvard Business Review, finding that 40% of 1,150 surveyed employees encountered workslop in just the past month, and that 95% of companies report no tangible return on their AI investments.

Using AI to measure and predict the depth of a consumer's ongoing emotional and behavioral connection to a brand, beyond repeat purchases.

Brand Stickiness Modeling analyzes behavioral data (visit frequency, dwell time, engagement), sentiment (social media and review tone), and engagement patterns across channels to model how strongly and durably a consumer stays connected to a brand. It matters for marketers because, unlike traditional loyalty programs that reward past transactions, stickiness models are predictive: they forecast future brand affinity and let brands adapt content and timing in real time to deepen emotional connection rather than just tracking points or purchases.

The concept is attributed to Jacqueline Woods, CMO of Teradata, introduced on Episode 25 of the Decoding AI for Marketers podcast, quoting her: "We help companies create deeper and more engaging experiences so they can become more sticky."

A future-focused alternative to feedback that offers constructive suggestions for what to do better next time instead of critiquing what already happened.

Feedforward replaces backward-looking evaluation (feedback) with forward-looking, solution-oriented guidance, for example saying "next time, keep your message shorter" instead of "your presentation was too long." It matters for marketing and leadership because it increases motivation and creativity in teams, shifts customer communication and campaign analysis from blame to improvement, and makes brands appear more innovative and trustworthy. The mindset connects directly to MMA Global's Project ROMI, which also focuses on forecasting the future business impact of marketing investment rather than only reporting past results.

Illustrative examples: reframing "this ad underperformed" as "in the next campaign, targeting Segment X can boost conversions," and reframing a past delivery problem as a promise of faster shipping next time.

The state in which an organization's complexity grows faster than its coordination, so activity rises while impact falls.

Structural chaos does not look like chaos: political shifts, economic pressure, and fragmented markets can look like growth until the system breaks. Its signature is more activity with less impact, because motion is not progress. The response the source proposes is resilience as strategy: anticipate, adapt, recover, align, and create value.

The practice of employees using their own, personally chosen AI tools at work without waiting for employer-provided or approved solutions.

BYOAI extends the older 'bring your own device' idea to generative AI. The term was popularized by the Microsoft and LinkedIn 2024 Work Trend Index, which found that 75% of knowledge workers used AI at work and 78% of those AI users brought their own tools. For marketing leaders it signals both demand and risk: teams are already experimenting, but unmanaged tools can expose customer and company data and fragment workflows, so the task is to provide sanctioned tools, training, and clear data rules.
A content team drafting campaign copy in personal ChatGPT accounts before the company has a licensed, governed AI tool is a typical BYOAI situation.

A blend of "senior" and "teenager" describing older adults, generally past traditional retirement age, who stay active, curious, and open to new trends.

Seenager describes people in their 60s, 70s, or beyond who reject the passive image often attached to old age and instead pursue travel, hobbies, fitness, and new experiences much as a teenager pursues novelty. The word began circulating online and in lifestyle press during the 2010s as a lighter, more positive alternative to labels like "senior citizen" or "elderly." Marketers read it as a signal: this age group wants to be treated as active consumers with disposable income and time, not as a passive demographic to be talked down to. Brands in travel, wellness, fashion, and technology increasingly build campaigns around this reframed image of later life.
Torun bakmak yerine yeni deneyimler arayan, aktif ve genç ruhlu yaşlı yetişkinleri tanımlamak için kullanılan "senior" ve "teenager" birleşiminden bir terim.
A blend of "queen" and "teenager" used for confident, stylish, middle-aged and older women who embrace their age rather than hide it.

Queenager was proposed by Alyson Walsh, journalist and founder of the style blog That's Not My Age, in a 2020 post arguing that older women deserve a more empowering label than "pensioner" or "OAP." The term reframes midlife and later life as a period of self-assurance and personal style rather than decline. The term names a large, high-spending demographic that fashion, beauty, and wellness brands have historically underserved or stereotyped; campaigns built around it position older women as aspirational rather than invisible.

That's Not My Age itself functions as a case study: Walsh built the blog and its "Queen-Ager" language into a recognized platform and community for stylish women over 50, which brands and retailers now reference when discussing this audience.
"Queen" (kraliçe) ve "teenager" kelimelerinin birleşiminden oluşan, yaşını saklamak yerine özgüvenle sahiplenen orta yaş ve üzeri kadınları tanımlayan terim.
A person who actively drives and supports the adoption of a new process, structure, or way of working inside an organization.

A change agent is an individual, inside or outside a company, who takes responsibility for making organizational change happen and stick, whether that is a new tool, a restructured team, or a shift in business model. The term is standard in management and organizational-development literature and is closely related to "change champion," though a change agent is generally seen as carrying more direct accountability for the change succeeding. Digital transformation, new martech adoption, or rebranding efforts typically fail without someone in this role who drives buy-in, training, and follow-through across departments.
Bir kuruluş içinde yeni bir süreç, yapı veya çalışma biçiminin benimsenmesini aktif olarak destekleyen ve yöneten kişi.
The set of principles and practices concerned with developing and using artificial intelligence in a safe, fair, and accountable way.

AI ethics addresses questions such as who is responsible for decisions an AI system makes, how to prevent bias and harm, and how to keep AI development aligned with human values. It has grown from an academic and policy discussion into a practical concern for any organization deploying AI, including marketers using generative tools, recommendation engines, or automated targeting. For marketing teams, misuse of customer data, biased personalization, or unchecked AI-generated content can create legal exposure and damage brand trust. Ethical review is now a normal part of AI adoption, not an afterthought.
Yapay zekanın güvenli, adil ve hesap verebilir biçimde geliştirilip kullanılmasını sağlayan ilke ve uygulamalar bütünü.
"Joy of Missing Out," the contentment that comes from opting out of social obligations or constant online activity, in contrast to FOMO.

JOMO was coined by writer Anil Dash in a 2012 blog post as a deliberate counterpoint to FOMO (fear of missing out), a term Patrick McGinnis had introduced in 2004. Where FOMO describes anxiety about missing events or updates, JOMO describes the relief and satisfaction of stepping back from that pressure and choosing presence over constant connectivity. The concept tracks a real consumer shift toward digital wellbeing, slower travel, and mindful consumption, and it has shaped campaigns in wellness, hospitality, and lifestyle categories that sell disconnection as a benefit rather than a loss.
Sürekli bağlantıda olma baskısından uzaklaşmanın verdiği huzuru ifade eden, FOMO'nun (bir şeyi kaçırma korkusu) karşıtı olan terim.
The habit of continuously scrolling through distressing or negative news and social media content, even when it causes anxiety.

Doomscrolling describes compulsively consuming a stream of alarming or negative information, usually through a smartphone, well past the point where it stops being informative and starts causing emotional harm. Usage of the term surged during the COVID-19 pandemic and periods of major news events, when 24-hour news cycles and algorithm-driven feeds made it easy to stay locked into distressing content. For marketers and platforms, it raises questions about content design, notification strategy, and audience wellbeing, and it has pushed some brands and apps toward messaging around digital breaks and healthier feed habits.
Kaygı veya sıkıntı yaratsa bile olumsuz haber ve sosyal medya içeriklerinde durmaksızın gezinme alışkanlığı.
A marketing approach that uses narrative techniques, rather than direct pitches, to sell products or services by building emotional connection.

Storyselling combines storytelling craft with a sales objective: instead of listing features, a brand builds a narrative with characters, tension, and resolution that leads the audience toward wanting the product. It draws on older ideas from advertising and copywriting about emotional persuasion, packaged under a term used mainly in marketing and sales-training content since the 2010s. Attention is scarce and consumers are skeptical of overt advertising, so a well-told story can carry a sales message further than a direct claim, particularly in video, social content, and brand campaigns.
Ürün veya hizmeti doğrudan anlatmak yerine hikaye anlatım teknikleriyle duygusal bağ kurarak satmayı amaçlayan pazarlama yaklaşımı.
A buying pattern where consumers research products online, then complete the purchase in a physical store.

ROBO, also called ROPO (research online, purchase offline) or webrooming, describes shoppers who compare prices, read reviews, and gather information online before buying in person, often to see or handle the product first or to avoid shipping delays. It is the mirror image of showrooming, where shoppers check a product in-store and then buy it online. For marketers, the pattern means online content, reviews, and search visibility directly influence in-store sales even when the final transaction leaves no online trail. That complicates attribution and makes omnichannel measurement harder to skip.
Tüketicilerin bir ürünü çevrimiçi araştırdıktan sonra fiziksel bir mağazadan satın aldığı alışveriş davranışı.
An informal, unpolished idea thrown out during brainstorming, offered for discussion rather than as a finished proposal.

To "spitball" is to suggest a rough idea without much preparation, typically in a casual or collaborative setting where the goal is to generate many possibilities rather than to present a fully developed plan. The term borrows from the literal meaning of a spitball as something quickly formed and thrown, used figuratively in business and creative jargon for informal idea generation. In marketing and creative teams, it signals psychological safety in brainstorming: team members are explicitly invited to share half-formed concepts without the pressure of immediate polish, and ideas that would otherwise go unsaid can surface.
Beyin fırtınası sırasında, henüz olgunlaşmamış ve tartışmaya açık olarak ortaya atılan gayriresmi bir fikir.
A discounted price or special offer given to customers who buy or register before a set deadline, used to drive early demand.

The early bird offer is a standard pricing tactic across events, travel, retail, and subscription businesses: buyers who commit early get a lower price or added benefit, while the brand gains early cash flow and demand signal well before the main sales period. It works on loss aversion and urgency, since customers who wait risk paying more or missing the deal entirely. For marketers, it is one of the most reliable levers for shaping the timing of demand, useful for events, product launches, and seasonal campaigns where predictable early sign-ups help with planning and cash flow.

Conference and event organizers commonly use early bird pricing tiers, for example offering a lower ticket price for registrations completed weeks before the event date, then raising the price as the date approaches.
Belirli bir son tarihten önce satın alan veya kaydolan müşterilere sunulan indirimli fiyat veya özel teklif.
The gap between curated, filtered, or manipulated media content and actual reality, especially as shaped by social media and retouched marketing imagery.

Distorted reality describes how heavily edited photos, selectively curated feeds, and idealized marketing visuals can create a false or exaggerated impression of a product, lifestyle, or person. The concept is not tied to one coiner; it has been discussed for years in media literacy and marketing-ethics writing as digital editing tools and social platforms made manipulation cheap and widespread. Consumers increasingly notice and react against unrealistic imagery, and brands that lean on authenticity and unretouched content often build more durable trust than those relying on idealized visuals.
Sosyal medya ve pazarlama görsellerindeki filtrelenmiş, rötuşlanmış içeriklerin gerçeklikle arasındaki farkı ifade eden kavram.
Brief, intent-driven moments when a person reaches for a device to know, go, do, or buy something, coined by Google in 2015.

Google introduced micro-moments in 2015 to describe the many short instances throughout a day when someone picks up a smartphone with a specific, immediate intent, whether that is looking up a fact, finding a nearby store, learning how to do something, or deciding what to buy. Google grouped these into "I-want-to-know," "I-want-to-go," "I-want-to-do," and "I-want-to-buy" moments. The concept shifted marketing planning away from broad demographic targeting toward being present and useful at the exact instant a consumer has a need, and it shaped mobile search, local SEO, and real-time content strategies.
Retailers optimize product pages and local listings for "near me" mobile searches specifically to capture I-want-to-go and I-want-to-buy micro-moments.
Google tarafından 2015 yılında tanımlanan, bir kişinin bir ihtiyacı karşılamak için cihazına yöneldiği kısa ve niyet dolu anlar.
A brand strategy that creates a sense of exclusive, insider access while still keeping the experience open to a broad and diverse audience.

Inclusive exclusivity describes retail and brand experiences designed to feel special and limited to those "in the know," while avoiding the elitism or narrowness of traditional exclusivity, by welcoming a diverse range of people who discover or opt into the experience. It is a marketing and retail-trend term rather than an academic one, used to describe things like invite-only drops, member communities, or pop-up experiences that use scarcity and insider language without excluding based on demographics. For marketers, it lets brands generate desire and community loyalty through perceived exclusivity while still growing an inclusive customer base, without the reputational risk of appearing elitist.
Markaların, ayrıcalık ve içeriden olma hissi yaratırken aynı zamanda geniş ve çeşitli bir kitleye açık kalan deneyimler kurgulaması.
Content sharing that happens through private channels like messaging apps and email, which standard web analytics cannot attribute to its true source.

Journalist Alexis Madrigal coined the term in a 2012 article for The Atlantic, after noticing that a large share of the site's traffic was logged as "direct" in analytics tools even though those visitors had actually arrived via links shared in private messages, chat apps, or email rather than by typing the URL directly. Because these referrals carry no tracking parameters, the true source of the traffic is invisible, hence "dark." A significant share of real sharing activity, often the most trusted kind, happens in these dark channels. Standard attribution models can undercount how content actually spreads and who is really driving conversions.
Doğrudan mesajlaşma veya e-posta gibi özel kanallar üzerinden yapılan, standart analitik araçlarla kaynağı tespit edilemeyen paylaşım biçimi.
When an AI system, especially a language model, confidently generates false or fabricated information that is not grounded in its training data or reality.

In its AI sense, to hallucinate means a system like a chatbot produces plausible-sounding but incorrect or invented content, such as fake citations, wrong facts, or nonexistent events, stated with the same confidence as accurate output. Cambridge Dictionary named "hallucinate" its Word of the Year for 2023 specifically because of this new AI-related meaning; the choice showed how central the issue had become as generative AI tools spread. For marketers using AI for copy, research, or customer-facing chat, unchecked hallucinations can put false claims or made-up statistics into published content. Outputs need fact-checking before use, or the result is legal and reputational risk.

Cambridge Dictionary's selection of "hallucinate" as its 2023 Word of the Year, tied directly to tools like ChatGPT producing confident but false statements, is the clearest documented example of this usage entering mainstream reference.
Bir yapay zeka sisteminin, özellikle dil modellerinin, gerçek olmayan veya uydurma bilgiyi kendinden emin bir şekilde üretmesi.
A marketing technique that uses popular internet memes and humor to promote a brand and connect with online audiences.

Memevertising, also called memetic marketing, involves brands adapting or referencing viral memes in their content to feel current, relatable, and shareable rather than promotional. It grew alongside the rise of meme culture on social platforms in the 2010s and is used mainly in social media marketing, where humor and cultural relevance can spread a message further than a conventional ad. For marketers, it can generate organic reach and audience goodwill cheaply, but it carries real risk: memes date quickly, and a brand using one poorly or too late can come across as forced or out of touch.
Bir markanın hedef kitlesiyle bağ kurmak için popüler internet memlerini ve mizahı kullandığı pazarlama tekniği.
The feeling of embarrassment or judgment an employee experiences when they have a technical problem at work, such as a video call glitch.

Tech shame describes the anxiety some employees feel about being seen as incompetent when they struggle with technology in front of colleagues, which can make them avoid speaking up in meetings or asking for help. A 2022 HP survey of 10,000 office workers, part of its "Hybrid Work: Are We There Yet?" report, found that one in five younger workers reported feeling this way, compared to about one in 25 older workers, roughly ten times the rate. For workplace and internal-communications teams, it points to a real barrier to participation and psychological safety, especially for younger employees in hybrid and remote-first teams.
HP's own "Hybrid Work: Are We There Yet?" survey report is the documented source of the one-in-five versus one-in-25 finding widely cited when the term is discussed.
Bir çalışanın, işte teknik bir sorun yaşadığında yargılanma korkusuyla hissettiği utanma duygusu.
An informal micro-generation label for people born around the cusp of Generation Z and Generation Alpha, blending traits of both cohorts.

Gen Zalpha is used to describe individuals, roughly those born in the mid-to-late 2000s to early 2010s, who share Gen Z's formative experience of social media's rise and Gen Alpha's status as full digital natives raised with even more advanced technology from birth. It is a marketing and commentary term rather than a formally defined demographic cohort from a research body like Pew, and different sources place its edges differently. For marketers targeting tweens and teens, this group blends behaviors from two adjacent generational frameworks, and some brands have specifically recruited "Gen Zalpha" influencer groups to reach both audiences at once.
Claire's, the accessories retailer, assembled a group of young influencers explicitly framed as "Gen Zalpha" brand ambassadors to guide creative direction aimed at both Gen Z and Gen Alpha shoppers.
Z Kuşağı ile Alpha Kuşağı arasındaki dönemde doğan, her iki kuşağın özelliklerini taşıyan kişileri tanımlayan gayriresmi terim.
A marketing acronym for Social, Local, and Mobile, describing strategies that combine these three elements to reach consumers.

SoLoMo was coined by venture capitalist John Doerr of Kleiner Perkins in 2010 to describe the convergence of social platforms, location-based data, and mobile devices as a single, powerful marketing trend. The idea was that smartphones, always carried and always connected, let brands combine social proof, geographic relevance, and mobile delivery in one targeted message, for example a location-based offer shared through a social app. Historically, it named an early wave of mobile-first, geo-targeted advertising that anticipated much of today's location-based and app-driven marketing, even though the term itself has faded from everyday use.
Sosyal, yerel ve mobil unsurları birleştirerek tüketiciye ulaşan pazarlama stratejilerini tanımlayan kısaltma.
A narrative technique that places the audience inside the story using technologies like VR, AR, or 360-degree video rather than having them observe from outside.

Immersive storytelling uses technologies such as virtual reality, augmented reality, 360-degree video, or interactive installations to make an audience feel present within a narrative instead of simply watching it unfold. It grew out of documentary and gaming experiments in the 2010s and has since been adopted in advertising, museum exhibits, and branded experiences. For marketers, it can create stronger emotional engagement and memorability than a traditional ad, though it requires more production investment and works best when the format genuinely serves the story rather than being used as a novelty.
Sanal gerçeklik, artırılmış gerçeklik veya 360 derece video gibi teknolojiler kullanarak izleyiciyi hikayenin içine dahil eden anlatım tekniği.
Two distinct workplace trends: quick quitting means leaving a job within roughly a year, while quiet quitting means staying in a role but doing only the minimum required.

Quick quitting refers to employees, often younger workers, leaving a job in under a year when it does not meet their expectations on pay, growth, or work-life balance, a pattern LinkedIn's Workforce Insights data showed rising in the early 2020s. Quiet quitting is a different behavior: staying employed but consciously stopping any effort beyond the defined job description, a term that went viral after engineer Zaid Khan posted a TikTok about it in July 2022, describing it as "quitting the idea of going above and beyond." Together, the two represent opposite responses to the same underlying dissatisfaction, one by physically leaving, the other by mentally disengaging while remaining on payroll, and both matter for people-management and internal-communications work.

Zaid Khan's July 2022 TikTok video, which popularized quiet quitting to a global audience and drew hundreds of millions of views under the #quietquitting hashtag, is the clearest documented origin point for that side of the comparison.
"Quick quitting" bir yıldan kısa sürede işten ayrılmayı, "quiet quitting" ise işte kalıp yalnızca gerekli asgari işi yapmayı ifade eder.
The practice of injecting a brand's message or perspective into a breaking news story to gain attention and media coverage.

Newsjacking was coined by marketer David Meerman Scott, who popularized it in his 2011 book of the same name, describing how brands can attach their own content or commentary to a trending news event to ride its existing attention. Done well, it means offering a genuinely relevant insight or reaction quickly while a story is still current; done poorly, it can look opportunistic or tone-deaf, especially around sensitive events. For marketers, it is one of the fastest ways to gain visibility without paid media, but it requires speed, editorial judgment, and sensitivity to avoid backlash.
Bir markanın mesajını, gündemdeki bir haberin dikkatinden yararlanmak için o habere dahil etme pratiği.
A business idiom meaning to make a noticeable, measurable, and usually positive impact toward a goal.

The phrase comes from the image of a needle on a gauge or meter shifting position in response to a change, and it is used in business to describe an action significant enough to produce a measurable result, as in "the new campaign moved the needle on sales." It functions as shorthand for meaningful progress as opposed to busywork or activity that looks productive but changes nothing measurable. The phrase is often used to set expectations for a campaign or initiative: stakeholders asking whether something will "move the needle" are really asking whether it is worth the investment given the size of impact it can realistically produce.
Bir hedefe doğru fark edilir ve ölçülebilir bir ilerleme kaydetmek anlamına gelen iş dünyası deyimi.
The degree to which an organization can effectively use digital technologies and processes to create value and respond to change.

Digital maturity measures how well a company has adopted the tools, skills, and culture needed to run digital-first processes, respond to market shifts, and pursue digital transformation, rather than treating digital as a bolt-on to existing operations. It is not a single achievement but an ongoing capability that consulting firms and technology vendors assess using various maturity models and frameworks. For marketing leadership, digital maturity level directly affects how fast a marketing team can adopt new channels, personalization, and data practices, and low maturity is a common reason ambitious campaigns underdeliver.
Bir kuruluşun dijital teknoloji ve süreçleri kullanarak değer yaratma ve değişime uyum sağlama kapasitesi.
Content that blends education and entertainment, designed to teach while also engaging and amusing the audience.

Edutainment is a portmanteau of "education" and "entertainment" used for games, films, shows, or digital experiences built to make learning engaging rather than dry. Walt Disney used the term as early as 1954 to describe the True-Life Adventure nature documentary series, and it has since expanded to cover eLearning platforms, branded content, and classroom technology. For marketers, especially in education, kids' products, and B2B thought leadership, content framed as edutainment tends to hold attention longer than a straightforward pitch while still delivering a brand or product message.
Walt Disney's True-Life Adventure documentary series in the 1950s is the earliest well-documented use of the term to describe entertainment built around educational content.
Eğitim ve eğlenceyi bir araya getirerek öğretirken aynı zamanda izleyiciyi eğlendirmeyi amaçlayan içerik türü.
A design and technology approach that delivers a consistent brand experience across many devices, senses, and interaction modes, such as touch, voice, and gesture.

Gartner named multiexperience one of its Top 10 Strategic Technology Trends for 2020, defining it as the shift from single-device thinking to a multisensory, multidevice, multimodal way people interact with the digital world, spanning web, mobile, wearables, voice assistants, and immersive interfaces. Rather than building one experience per channel, organizations aim for a cohesive journey regardless of which touchpoint a customer uses. A fragmented experience across channels damages brand perception and conversion, so multiexperience thinking forces marketing and product teams to coordinate content and interaction design across every surface a customer might use.
Dokunma, ses ve hareket gibi birçok etkileşim biçimi ve cihaz üzerinden tutarlı bir marka deneyimi sunan tasarım ve teknoloji yaklaşımı.
A cultural sensibility positioned between modernism's sincerity and postmodernism's irony, now applied in marketing to describe brand tones that mix earnestness with self-aware humor.

Cultural theorists Timotheus Vermeulen and Robin van den Akker introduced metamodernism in their 2010 essay "Notes on Metamodernism," describing a cultural mood that oscillates between modernist hope and postmodern irony rather than settling into either. In marketing commentary, the term has been adapted to describe campaigns that combine optimism, honesty, and humor, appealing especially to Gen Z and Gen Alpha audiences who are wary of both naive positivity and cynical detachment. For marketers, it offers language for a tone that has become common in youth-focused advertising: sincere but self-aware, hopeful but not saccharine.
Modernizmin samimiyeti ile postmodernizmin ironisi arasında salınan, artık pazarlamada içtenlik ve mizahı birleştiren marka tonlarını tanımlamak için de kullanılan kültürel yaklaşım.
The observation that people tend to overestimate the short-term impact of a new technology and underestimate its long-term impact.

Amara's Law is attributed to Roy Amara, a researcher and futurist who served as president of the Institute for the Future, and is generally dated to around 1978. It captures a recurring pattern: a new technology generates a wave of hype and inflated short-term expectations, followed by a period of disappointment, before its real, often larger, impact plays out over a longer timeframe than initial excitement suggested. For marketers and technology leaders, it is a useful check on campaign and product planning around emerging technology, such as AI or AR: it warns against both overpromising immediate results and dismissing a technology too early because it has not yet delivered on hype.
İnsanların yeni bir teknolojinin kısa vadeli etkisini abartıp uzun vadeli etkisini hafife alma eğilimini ifade eden gözlem.
An adult consumer who buys toys, games, or collectibles for personal enjoyment rather than for a child, driven by nostalgia and hobbyist interest.

Kidult blends "kid" and "adult" and is used in the toy and collectibles industry for grown consumers, often collectors, who purchase items like construction sets, action figures, or trading cards for themselves. Industry reporting puts kidults at roughly a quarter of annual toy sales, with brands such as Lego expanding product lines specifically toward adult builders seeking complex, nostalgic sets. For marketers in toys, entertainment, and licensed merchandise, this audience buys based on nostalgia, craftsmanship, and franchise attachment rather than child-appropriate play value, and it needs different messaging and pricing than traditional toy marketing.
Lego's expansion into large, intricate adult-targeted sets tied to franchises like Star Wars is a widely cited example of a brand building a product line specifically for kidult consumers.
Bir çocuk için değil kendi keyfi için oyuncak, koleksiyon parçası veya oyun satın alan yetişkin tüketici.
A verb, popularized mainly by millennials, describing the act of doing routine responsible tasks associated with being a grown-up.

Adulting refers humorously to completing ordinary adult responsibilities, like paying bills or doing laundry, framed as an accomplishment worth acknowledging, often with the hashtag #adulting. The modern usage grew out of social media around 2008-2009 and was significantly boosted by Kelly Williams Brown's 2013 book "Adulting: How to Become a Grown-Up in 468 Easy(ish) Steps," with the word entering Urban Dictionary in 2014 and seeing a major surge in use by 2016. For marketers targeting millennial and Gen Z audiences, brands, including major companies, have used "adulting" language in campaigns to speak to young adults navigating delayed milestones like homeownership or marriage with self-aware humor rather than a serious, aspirational tone.
Kelly Williams Brown's 2013 book "Adulting" is the clearest documented driver of the word's mainstream spread beyond internet slang.
Genellikle Y kuşağı tarafından yaygınlaştırılan, yetişkinliğe özgü sıradan sorumlulukları yerine getirmeyi ifade eden mizahi terim.
A packaged piece of knowledge, such as an online course, ebook, or template, sold or reused repeatedly instead of being created fresh each time.

An information product is expertise or research turned into a reusable, sellable format, for example an online course, guide, template, or report, that can be delivered to many customers with little additional effort once created. In creator-economy and digital-marketing contexts, this model lets a person or company convert knowledge built for one purpose into a scalable offering, and it can also mean adapting an existing information product to a similar new request rather than starting from scratch. For marketers and consultants, it turns expertise into a repeatable revenue stream, and it lowers the barrier for less experienced people to present themselves credibly once they have a well-packaged product to point to.
Bilgi veya uzmanlığı, tekrar tekrar satılabilen bir çevrimiçi kurs, e-kitap ya da şablon gibi paketlenmiş bir ürüne dönüştüren kavram.
The practice of exaggerating or falsely claiming a product's or company's use of artificial intelligence to appear more innovative than it actually is.

AI washing describes marketing and investor communications that overstate a company's actual AI capabilities, similar to how greenwashing overstates environmental credentials. US regulators, including the SEC, adopted the term around 2023-2024 after bringing enforcement actions against firms that misrepresented their AI use to investors. Marketers face real exposure here: describing ordinary automation or rules-based software as AI-powered, without substance behind the claim, creates legal and reputational risk.
In 2024 the SEC settled its first AI washing charges against investment advisers Delphia and Global Predictions for making false claims about their use of artificial intelligence in client materials.

Bir şirketin ya da ürünün yapay zeka kullanımını gerçekte olduğundan daha ileri düzeyde göstererek abartılı veya yanıltıcı iddialarda bulunmasıdır.
A philosophical and social movement that uses evidence and reasoning to determine the most effective ways to help others and allocate resources.

Effective altruism emerged in the early 2010s, associated with philosophers William MacAskill and Toby Ord at Oxford and influenced by Peter Singer's writing on global poverty and ethics. It asks donors, volunteers, and organizations to prioritize actions by measurable impact per dollar or hour rather than by emotional appeal alone. Brands running cause campaigns or CSR programs feel this shift already: audiences, especially younger and more skeptical consumers, increasingly expect proof of measurable impact rather than feel-good messaging.
Effective altruism principles influenced the founding of GiveWell, a nonprofit that evaluates charities by cost-effectiveness so donors can direct money to the highest-impact causes.
Corporate Social Responsibility, Impact Measurement, Cause Marketing
Kaynakların ve yardımın en somut ve ölçülebilir faydayı sağlayacak şekilde, kanıta dayalı olarak yönlendirilmesini savunan felsefi ve toplumsal harekettir.
The anxiety that individuals or organizations feel about falling behind if they do not quickly adopt artificial intelligence tools.

FOMA is a recent coinage that plays on the older FOMO (fear of missing out), applied specifically to pressure around AI adoption. It surfaced in marketing and workplace commentary as generative AI tools spread rapidly after 2023, and has since been studied by academics examining workplace anxiety about AI skill gaps and job security, sometimes labeled AI FOMO in that research. FOMA matters to marketers in two ways: it explains why clients and leadership push for AI-labeled products even without a clear use case, and it is itself a psychological trigger that some AI vendors intentionally use in their own marketing.

Recent workplace research on AI FOMO identifies distinct anxiety dimensions, including fear of skill obsolescence and fear of being excluded from AI-driven decisions, that echo the FOMA framing used in marketing commentary.
Yapay zekayı hızla benimsemeyen kişi veya kurumların geride kalma korkusunu ifade eden bir terimdir.
The current era of technological change in which digital, physical, and biological systems are merging through AI, robotics, and connected devices.

The term was coined by Klaus Schwab, founder of the World Economic Forum, who introduced it at the 2016 Davos meeting and expanded on it in a book of the same name. It builds on the historical framing of three prior industrial revolutions, steam and mechanization, electricity and mass production, electronics and computing, to describe today's convergence of AI, IoT, biotechnology, and automation. The concept matters to marketing teams because it frames how consumer behavior, supply chains, and media consumption are being reshaped simultaneously by multiple overlapping technologies rather than by a single innovation.
Klaus Schwab used the World Economic Forum's annual Davos meeting to popularize the term, arguing it would change not only what people do but who they are.
Yapay zeka, robotik ve bağlantılı cihazların dijital, fiziksel ve biyolojik sistemleri birleştirdiği günümüz teknolojik dönüşüm çağını tanımlayan terimdir.
The disruption of a traditional service industry by digital platforms that connect customers and providers directly, bypassing established intermediaries.

The term derives from Uber, whose app-based, on-demand ride-hailing model became shorthand for a broader pattern: digital platforms matching supply and demand in real time without the fixed schedules, ownership structures, or intermediaries of the industry they replace. The word gained particular traction in France before spreading internationally. Uberisation matters to marketers because it signals which categories are vulnerable to platform disruption and reframes competitive strategy around access and convenience rather than ownership.

Beyond transportation, the term is commonly applied to sectors like food delivery, freelance labor platforms, and home services, where an app-based intermediary replaces the traditional agency or storefront model.
Dijital platformların, müşteri ve hizmet sağlayıcıyı doğrudan buluşturarak geleneksel aracıları devre dışı bırakmasıyla bir sektörün dönüşmesini ifade eder.
A model of work in which organizations source labor on demand from a global pool of independent, digitally connected workers rather than fixed employees.

The term human cloud was adopted by staffing industry analysts to describe digitally enabled work arrangements covering everything from sourcing a worker to paying them. It is a subset of the broader gig economy, encompassing online staffing, crowdsourcing, and online work services. Fluid workforce is used interchangeably to describe the same shift toward flexible, project-based talent. The model changes how marketing and brand leaders staff creative, analytics, and campaign work, often blending in-house teams with distributed freelance talent sourced through platforms.

HR and staffing platforms such as Business Talent Group and KellyOCG market human cloud solutions that let companies tap independent professionals for discrete projects instead of hiring full-time staff.
Gig Economy, Platform Economy, Contingent Workforce
Kurumların sabit çalışanlar yerine dijital platformlar aracılığıyla talebe göre bağımsız işgücünden yararlanmasını tanımlayan bir çalışma modelidir.
A transitional phase in which the potential of a new technology, such as AI, is widely recognized but not yet fully understood or put to productive use.

The between times is a descriptive phrase rather than a term with a single credited coiner; it is used in technology and marketing commentary to name the awkward middle period after a breakthrough technology is announced but before organizations have built the skills, processes, and trust to use it well. Applied to AI, it captures the current moment where most companies have access to generative AI tools but have not yet redesigned workflows or measurement around them. Naming this phase helps marketers explain the gap between AI hype and AI return on investment, and it sets realistic expectations for adoption timelines.
The phrase is commonly used in AI strategy discussions to caution leadership against over- or under-investing in AI while the organization is still in this in-between adoption stage.

Yeni bir teknolojinin, örneğin yapay zekanın, potansiyelinin tanınmasına rağmen henüz tam olarak anlaşılıp verimli biçimde kullanılamadığı geçiş dönemini ifade eder.
An AI safety vulnerability in which attackers use long prompts filled with many example dialogues to trick a large language model into bypassing its safety guardrails.

Anthropic researchers disclosed many-shot jailbreaking in 2024, showing that expanded context windows, which let models process much longer prompts, can be exploited by inserting a large number of simulated question-and-answer exchanges that gradually lead the model toward producing harmful content. The technique works because it takes advantage of in-context learning, the same ability that makes long-context models more useful for legitimate tasks. Anthropic found that hardening models through fine-tuning only increased the number of shots needed, while modifying the prompt itself was more effective at reducing the attack's success rate. The finding matters to brands deploying AI chatbots or generative tools: longer context windows widen both capability and attack surface, making safety testing essential before public deployment.

Anthropic disclosed the technique to other AI labs and researchers ahead of publishing its findings, and has continued researching mitigations such as classifying and limiting suspicious long-context prompts before they reach the model.
Prompt Injection, LLM Jailbreak, In-Context Learning, AI Safety
Saldırganların, çok sayıda örnek diyalog içeren uzun bir istemle büyük dil modellerinin güvenlik korumalarını atlatmaya çalıştığı bir yapay zeka güvenlik açığıdır.
The practice of structuring and optimizing brand content so that generative AI tools and chatbots cite, reference, or recommend it in their answers.

GAIO extends the logic of search engine optimization to a world where consumers increasingly get answers from AI systems like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Bing Chat instead of a list of search results. Rather than optimizing for keyword rankings and backlinks, GAIO focuses on clarity, structure, and factual consistency so AI models are more likely to surface, paraphrase, or cite a brand's content as a trustworthy source. The discipline is still emerging and terminology is not fully settled, with related labels such as AEO (Answer Engine Optimization) and GEO (Generative Engine Optimization) used by different practitioners for similar practices. Being invisible to AI answer engines increasingly means being invisible to the customer at the point of decision, which is why GAIO matters to marketers.

Marketing agencies now audit brand content for GAIO readiness, checking whether product pages and articles are structured clearly enough for an AI model to extract and cite accurate information rather than an outdated or third-party source.
SEO, AEO (Answer Engine Optimization), GEO (Generative Engine Optimization), E-E-A-T
Marka içeriğinin, üretken yapay zeka araçları tarafından yanıtlarda alıntılanacak veya önerilecek şekilde yapılandırılması ve optimize edilmesi pratiğidir.
An AI-powered mentor tool from MMA Global (Marketing + Media Alliance) that helps marketers choose categories and prepare stronger entries for the SMARTIES Awards.

The SMARTIES Awards are MMA Global's awards program recognizing innovation and effectiveness in mobile and digital marketing. SMARTIES Coach is a generative AI assistant, built as a custom GPT experience, that guides entrants through selecting the right award category, explains what judges look for, shares examples from past winners, and walks users through submission requirements and deadlines. The tool lowers the barrier to crafting a competitive submission for marketers preparing award entries, and reflects MMA's own use of AI to support its member community.
Marketers preparing a SMARTIES entry can consult SMARTIES Coach on mmaglobal.com to get category recommendations and guidance before submitting their campaign for judging.
SMARTIES Awards, MMA Global, Award Submission Strategy
